Split paired values reported in one cell

Source: R/split.R
split_iqr.Rd

Studies often report an interquartile range or a range as a single cell, e.g. "2, 5" or "[2.5; 7]". split_iqr() returns the first and third quartiles and split_range() the minimum and maximum. Cells that do not hold exactly two numbers give NA for both.

Usage

split_iqr(x, ..., sep = default_pair_sep())

split_range(x, ..., sep = default_pair_sep())

Arguments

x

Character vector of paired values.

...

Unused; must be empty.

sep

Regular expression separating the two values. The default accepts commas, semicolons, " to " and en or em dashes. Hyphens are not split on by default because they clash with negative numbers; use sep = "\\s+-\\s+" for values like "2 - 5".

Value

A tibble with one row per element of x and columns q1 and q3 (split_iqr()) or min and max (split_range()).

Examples

split_iqr(c("2, 5", "[1.5; 3]", "4 to 9", "7"))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>      q1    q3
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1   2       5
#> 2   1.5     3
#> 3   4       9
#> 4  NA      NA
split_range("0 to 12")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>     min   max
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     0    12
